findings: gradient_rules contradicts the idea and the spec's own mechanism: the entry 'the cost C[i,k] and the plan P' states 'no gradient: they are DECISION variables', while the idea requires 'gradients flow only through v_i and u_k', the mechanism states 'the reconstruction's gradient reaches the cost and, through it, the fine levels' CODEBOOK rows u_k', the `excluded` list says the effect 'runs through the plan's straight-through estimator', and displaced_code/distance/sinkhorn_plan are flagged "differentiable": true. The gradient rule must instead state that C and P are differentiable, that the reconstruction gradient reaches u_k through q_{i,k} = u_k (+)_c Delta_i with Delta_i and the field detached, and that the plan is the baseline's straight-through path; the 'DECISION variables / no gradient' rule must be deleted.

Two mutually exclusive straight-through estimators are given for the same quantity. The mechanism says x_q = P + (one_hot(k_l(i)) - P).detach(); its forward value is one_hot(k_l(i)), NOT the chosen raw codeword, so the accompanying claim 'the forward value is exactly the baseline's' is false, and its backward gives the gradient to P (hence C and u_k). computations.quantised_value instead defines e_l = r + (a_k - r).detach(), whose forward value is the raw codeword a_k but whose backward carries no gradient into C at all. The spec must state ONE estimator whose forward value is the chosen raw codeword a_{k_l(i)} and whose backward carries the reconstruction gradient into C (e.g. x_q = sum_k P_ik a_k + (a_k - sum_k P_ik a_k).detach()), and the forward-value claim must match it.

The curvature used to build the behaviour field is not pinned down in the computations that define it. successor_snapshot, ball_lift, code_lift and nearest_code_distance all declare the same switchable input 'c' and are written with exp_0^c / d_c, yet switch_geometry (and the switches/ablations text) states the field is 'computed with the CURVED operators (c = 1) in BOTH arms'. As declared, GEOM=euclid would flatten the snapshot V_l, the code points used by d_nn_i, and hence m_i, contradicting the claim that the two arms 'differ in ... nothing else'. Only the private constant c_field inside continuous_surface.executable_statements preserves the field; the per-computation definitions must use a frozen field curvature c = 1 (c_field) for V_l, u^field_k, log_{v_i} and d_nn_i, with the switchable c applied only to the cost's lift, Möbius sum and distance.

The note of nearest_code_distance ('It equals the BEHAV=off cost row minimum') and the arc_length note ('it keeps the displacement shorter than half the distance to the nearest code') are false under GEOM=euclid: there the field's d_nn_i stays the curved d_c (as the switch requires) while the BEHAV=off cost is the flat d_0(x,y) = 2||x-y||, so the two numbers are different metrics of the same pair and the cap guarantees nothing about the flat cost. The notes must be restricted to the curved arm, or d_nn_i must be stated as the curved cap used in both arms with no equality claim to the euclid cost.

The 'outputs' list promises four diagnostics — the offset of the displacement, the per-code usage of the fine levels, the number of distinct level-2 prefixes and the three-level collision — and no computation defines any of them (no definition of the offset magnitude, of the usage histogram, of the prefix count or of the collision rate appears in 'computations'). Either the four diagnostic computations must be added with their exact formulas and the split they are measured on, or the outputs entry must be removed.
reason: The geometry itself is faithful and numerically correct (the lift, the Möbius sum, the log map, the artanh clip, d_c(0,Delta_i)=m_i with the framework's factor 2, the frozen q_l, the BEHAV=off collapse and the GEOM=euclid limits all match the idea and its recorded correction). It must nevertheless be revised: (1) gradient_rules denies the very gradient path the idea requires and kills the codebook route through the displaced cost, contradicting the mechanism, the excluded list and its own differentiability flags; (2) two incompatible straight-through estimators are given, one of which also mis-states its forward value; (3) the field's curvature is left switchable in the snapshot and the nearest-code cap, so the euclid arm would not be the matched control the switches claim; (4) the nearest-code cap note claims an equality that fails in the euclid arm; (5) four promised diagnostics are never defined.
